meta.title: NUMBER ONE — POLIJE × KNU, Jember 2026
meta.description: 2026 WFK IT Volunteer Corps, Team NUMBER ONE, Kyungpook National University. Nine people from Korea and Indonesia built and shipped PlantMoji, a smart-farming learning game, during 22 days in Jember.
hero.eyebrow: 2026 WFK IT Volunteer Corps · KNU Team NUMBER ONE
hero.lede: We were in Jember, Indonesia for 22 days, from 27 July to 17 August 2026. Five students from Politeknik Negeri Jember (POLIJE) and four from Kyungpook National University (KNU), one team. Farming knowledge mostly passes from person to person. We wanted to put it into data so the next generation could pick it up, so we built PlantMoji.
hero.livenow: Open it right now · running as of 25 Aug 2026
philos.title: Wisdom into data, data into the next generation
philos.lede: Farming in Jember still runs on intuition. But that intuition is not guessing. It is wisdom built over generations. We set out to carry it forward with technology.
philos.s1.title: Experience
philos.s1.body: When to water, what the soil wants — a farmer in Jember knows it by hand. Decades of experience. But only 22% of farmers are millennials, and unrecorded instinct leaves with its generation.
philos.s2.title: Data
philos.s2.body: The sensor does not replace that instinct. It only writes down, in numbers, what the instinct already knew. Soil moisture, temperature, humidity, light, pH — the things a farmer has always measured by hand. Once they are on record, that judgement can reach someone who never stood in the same field.
philos.s3.title: The next generation
philos.s3.body: Even a student who has never farmed can start with joy, through play. Clearing quests, earning XP, filling the collection — and along the way, water, soil and light become second nature. Time that begins as fun becomes time spent learning agriculture.
philos.quote: PlantMoji is here to carry farming wisdom forward — to the next generation.
legacy.title: What stayed after we left
legacy.lede: Volunteering usually ends when the trip ends. We wanted what we left behind to keep running.
legacy.s3.title: Left in a form that can be picked up
legacy.s3.body: We left code, not slides. Three public repositories, migration scripts that can rebuild the database from scratch, and documentation written in English, Indonesian and Korean. There are tests, too, so a mistake shows itself right away. A POLIJE student next semester can open the repository and continue from today.
team.title:
One team — under one sky — indivisible,
with wisdom and technology, for the next generation.
team.lede: Nine of us shared four roles — PL, TL, KL and ML. Each school held one of each, so PL worked paired with PL, and TL with TL. Every one of us was a builder.
team.role.PL.desc: Merged two campuses into one schedule and decided what came first each day. Every call was closed with both sides in the room.
team.role.TL.desc: Designed and built the path the data travels, from sensor to web app to mobile. Most of the 280 commits came from these hands.
team.role.KL.desc: Decided at which reading the plant gets thirsty and what each quest should teach. The role that wrote the answer key of the game.
team.role.ML.desc: Jamkachu, 300 sprites, the shop items, the decks and the Instagram — everything the team is seen through.
shipped.title: What we shipped
shipped.lede: These are the things we built and shipped. Two of them you can open right now.
shipped.web.name: PlantMoji web app
shipped.web.tagline: Sensor readings become a mood, and the mood becomes a quest.
shipped.web.body: A sensor reading turns into a plant's mood, and that mood issues a care quest. When you actually water the plant, the next reading verifies it, and success pays out XP, bond levels and badges. The mascot is called Jamkachu, after Jember.
shipped.mobile.name: Mobile PlantEmoji
shipped.mobile.tagline: We did not stop at the web — we shipped a mobile app too.
shipped.mobile.body: Five Flutter screens poll the PlantMoji backend every ten seconds. The plant sprite grows through four stages driven by the level the server computes, and the mood collection and grow diary share the same state as the web app. The camera scan re-encodes JPEG at quality 72, 60, 48 and 36 until the upload fits a 195 KB budget.
shipped.mobile.note: The web app and the mobile app share one game state. Care for the plant from either one and the same progress carries over.
shipped.design.name: Pixel farm design & UI/UX
shipped.design.tagline: What we drew became the product itself.
shipped.design.body: Reno's cozy pixel-farm layout did not stay a reference. It became the actual home screen of the web app — the shell component is named reno-app-shell, and the handover document fixes that design as the immutable visual source of truth. Our teammate Kiki drew the plant sprites across four growth stages and five moods, eight mood badges, and six NPCs. Our teammate Suhyeon Park owned UI/UX across the product, designing all 31 shop items and Jamkachu's speech bubbles, and reworking every screen that did not sit right in the hand.
shipped.design.note: Two cultures sit side by side in the shop — a taegeuk ribbon and a mugunghwa next to a batik pot, a JFC headdress, and a Jember tobacco barn. The colours and pixel feel of this page come from that same design system.
shipped.camera.name: Camera AI
shipped.camera.tagline: An image classifier that runs inside the browser.
shipped.camera.body: A two-class model with a MobileNetV2 backbone runs directly in the browser and re-classifies the view every 2.5 seconds. Below 0.70 confidence it declines to give a verdict at all. The video never leaves the device.
shipped.nodered.name: PlantMoji decision engine
shipped.nodered.tagline: So the plant survives a dropped sensor and a forgetful owner.
shipped.nodered.body: This is where a sensor reading turns into how the plant feels. When a value wavers on the boundary, separate thresholds for on and off keep the plant's expression from flickering with it, and gaps in the data earn no points. When a sensor goes quiet, the system notices before a person does.
shipped.nodered.note: There are six feelings — happy, thirsty, too hot, sleepy, soil gone sour, soil gone salty.
codev.title: Proof that we built it together
codev.lede: This collaboration is written into the commit log. Who changed whose code, and when — you can verify it right now in three public repositories.
codev.org.label: Where the repositories live
codev.org.desc: Both institutions are written into the organisation name. All three repositories are public.
codev.dir1.label: Main-PlantMoji
codev.dir1.desc: Our teammate Reno put the Camera AI model he retrained in the field straight into the web app codebase. The background-music system came from the same hands.
codev.dir2.label: Mobile-PlantEmoji
codev.dir2.desc: Our teammate Jinseok Seo wired the Flutter app to the PlantMoji APIs and made bond level and sensor state actually show up.
codev.shared.label: One shared state
codev.shared.desc: The mobile app's /api/* calls go to the same server as the web app. Both screens see the same level, XP and streak.
retrain.eyebrow: The scene that explains this team
retrain.title: We retrained it in the field
retrain.lede: What we built got it wrong in a real greenhouse. So before we packed up and flew home, we trained it again on site.
retrain.step1.title: First training
retrain.step1.body: We trained and exported the image classifier on location in Jember.
retrain.step2.title: Wrong in the real greenhouse
retrain.step2.body: The growing environment did not look like the scene we had trained on, and the model would not call a safe environment safe.
retrain.step3.title: Retrained and redeployed
retrain.step3.body: We trained it again on site and shipped it into the product. The backbone stayed; only the classifier changed.
retrain.viz.title: What actually changed
retrain.viz.caption: Of 263 weight tensors, 3 changed — all of them in the classifier head. The 410,208 backbone parameters were left alone; only the part that makes the judgement was taught again.

ground.lede: We spent 22 days in Jember. Between building, we ran cultural exchange events, visited a school, and met people.

philos.roots: Polije is a school with its own line of agricultural IT research — Smart Green House, Agribot SIP. Within that current toward smart farming, we built PlantMoji together, in a form any classroom can touch.
wins.title: First place twice, out of nine teams
wins.lede: Nine teams from the KNU cohort competed under the same conditions. We came first in the Arduino project and in K-Food Day — and the ranking came from Jember, not from us.
wins.w1.title: Arduino project
wins.w1.body: We demonstrated the full pipeline live, from sensor kit to web app, and were judged on the system working right there.
wins.w2.title: K-Food Day
wins.w2.judge: Participant vote + faculty scoring + Reels likes
wins.w2.body: Earned with a booth where we made and shared hwachae and es buah together.
wins.w3.title: KBS DOCU-ON broadcast
wins.w3.body: DOCU-ON, a documentary programme of KBS — Korea's public broadcaster — filmed Team NUMBER ONE's activities throughout the deployment.
ground.smk.title: SMK Negeri 4 Jember
ground.smk.body: The scheduled programme was a K-performance only. We proposed a PlantMoji session, and after discussion with the school it was added to the official schedule. For an hour, the students cared for Jamkachu themselves and worked with live sensor data.
ground.smk.note: It was the day PlantMoji first reached the next generation's hands.
legacy.s4.title: Still running
legacy.s4.body: The web app and the mobile app are still on after the deployment ended. The collection and the grow diary hold the records built up in Jember, and the address works the moment you open it. The buttons at the top of this page are that address.
footer.slogan: One Team. One Vision. Infinite Impact.

legacy.s1.title: People who can build it stayed
legacy.s1.body: Nine of us built PlantMoji together, and five are still in Jember. They raised this system from the first line, so they can fix it — and grow it.
legacy.s2.title: The collaboration did not end at the airport
legacy.s2.body: Working in the same repositories became a habit. With an ocean in between, the code still lands in one place, and we can see each other's commits today.
legacy.snaps.title: Moments saved in the grow diary
legacy.snaps.body: These were taken with PlantMoji's camera in Jember and saved into the grow diary. The students gathered in front of the lens, and the strawberry planted in the kit — they are all in there. Open the diary today and they still are.
